title: Ask Genie Anywhere | Bring AI/BI Genie to Microsoft Teams & M365 Copilot via Copilot Studio
transcriptText:
What if you could answer your data
questions directly in the collaboration
tools that you use every day?
Hi everyone. My name is Hamlin and I'm a
product manager for AI BI Genie at
Databricks. Genie is a data analyst
agent that lets you simply talk to your
data and get insights, all powered by
the unique knowledge of your data
intelligence platform.
One request we kept hearing from our
customers was we want to bring Genie
into our Microsoft collaboration
environments like Teams, SharePoint, or
M365.
To help with this, we're excited to
launch Genie's native integration with
Copilot Studio. This lets your
organization seamlessly bring a Genie
space into your collaboration tools so
your users can answer their data
questions the moment they come up in
conversations without leaving the flow
of work.
I'll now hand it over to Toussaint who
will take us through a demo of bringing
a Genie space into Copilot Studio and
publishing it to your Microsoft Teams.
Thanks, Hamlin. My name is Toussaint and
I'm a product manager on the partner
ecosystem team. Where I focus on making
Databricks' capabilities available in
our partner solutions.
But enough about me.
Let's jump into the demo.
Imagine you've created a Genie space
powered by Unity Catalog designed to
deliver precise answers about your
product sales.
And now you want to bring that
capability directly into Teams for your
business users. The first step is
connecting your Databricks workspace to
Power Platform. To do this, open Power
Apps,
click connections,
select new connection,
and choose either Azure Databricks or
Databricks depending upon whether you
are using Databricks on Azure or on AWS
and GCP.
For this demo, I will use Azure
Databricks.
When creating the connection, you can
choose how to authenticate into your
Databricks workspace.
You have the choice of OAuth or service
principal.
Choose OAuth when you want users to sign
in as themselves with their own identity
and permissions.
Use a service principal when you want
the app to run under a shared
system-level identity for more
controlled or automated access.
I will use OAuth. To get the connection
details, the server host name, and HTTP
path,
open your Databricks workspace,
navigate to SQL warehouses,
select the desired SQL warehouse,
and open the connection details.
Once you've copied this information
over, you can create the connection.
Now that your Databricks workspace is
connected to Power Platform, the next
step is to bring Genie to a Copilot
Studio agent.
In Copilot Studio,
you can choose to either create a new
agent or select an existing agent.
After selecting an agent, it is time to
connect my desired Genie space.
To do this, open the tools page,
click add a tool,
and under the MCP section, choose
between either Azure Databricks Genie or
Databricks Genie.
This is the configuration step and it is
very simple for you.
Our integration handles all of the MCP
and API logic, so all you have to do is
remember the name of your Genie space.
Additionally, as part of this
configuration step, you can choose how
you want end users to authenticate into
the Genie space. You have the option
between end user credentials or maker
provided credentials.
Select end user credentials if you want
each person to run questions using their
own data permissions.
Choose maker provided credentials when
you want all questions to run under a
single service identity that you can
control and monitor.
Click save,
and we can confirm that the connection
was successful by refreshing the tools
description.
Let's try again.
Perfect.
After connecting Genie to your Copilot
Studio agent, there are a few optional
steps that you can take to make the
integration as performant and reliable
as possible.
First, open your agent settings page,
and confirm that it is using generative
AI for orchestration.
This will help your Copilot Studio agent
intelligently decide when to call Genie
as a tool.
Second, if you selected end user
credentials, we recommend enable
connection parameter sharing.
This will ensure that each end user is
using the correct host name and HTTP
path when authenticating.
To do this, under the connection, click
see details,
connection parameters, and allow
permission to share parameters.
Third,
open your agent's overview page,
and select Claude Sonnet 4.5 as the
model for your Copilot Studio agent.
We have found that this model performs
best when calling Genie as a tool.
Finally, we recommend adding clear and
concise instructions for your Copilot
Studio agent that describe when and how
it should query your Genie space,
helping ensure that your users
consistently get accurate answers.
The final step is to make the
Genie-enabled Copilot Studio agent
available where your users are.
Genie-enabled agents can be published to
any Microsoft channel including Teams,
M365 Copilot, or SharePoint.
To do this, you first need to publish
your agent.
Now that the agent is published,
open the channels tab,
and select Teams and M365 Copilot as the
channel.
Click add channel.
It's asking me to publish again.
Perfect.
At this point, we've successfully
connected your Databricks workspace to
Power Platform, added Genie as a tool to
your Copilot Studio agent, published
your Copilot Studio agent, and added the
Genie-enabled agent to Teams and M365
Copilot. Now your stakeholders can start
getting trusted insights from Genie
directly within Teams or M365 Copilot.
Let's see this in action.
Click see agent in Teams,
open Teams,
and you will be prompted to add the
agent.
I have previously added my agent to my
Teams workspace, so I'm being asked to
open it.
Now we can start conversing with the
Genie-enabled agent.
Perfect. Let's ask a follow-up question.
What's happening is that Copilot Studio
is taking the question that I've asked,
sending it to Genie,
Genie is performing an analysis,
and then will return the response to
Copilot Studio.
At that time, Copilot Studio is doing
some formatting before returning the
response to me.
And let's try one more question.
Perfect.
And with this quick demo, you can
already start to see the power of this
integration.
We've brought the trusted insights of
Genie directly into Teams, the interface
where your business users do business.
The last thing that I want to call out
is that all conversations remain fully
auditable through the Genie interface,
ensuring transparency and trust.
So as you just saw, it is very easy and
seamless to connect Genie to a Copilot
Studio agent, and ultimately publish
that agent to your desired channel,
whether Teams, M365 Copilot, or
SharePoint.
This integration brings Genie's trusted
insights into the interfaces where your
users already work,
helping everyone make smarter and faster
decisions.
If you want to learn more and find
step-by-step guidance on how to set this
up, check out the blog link in the
captions.
Thank you all for listening,
and have a good day.
>> [music]
